issues: Nothing suggests an attempt to get around the measurement. The diff adds one new kind of late restart: rotate the best packing by 2 to 6 degrees about the centre, add small noise drawn from the seeded rng, shrink the radii by 5 percent, then run SLSQP again. It reads no files, pastes no coordinates and does not use the test inputs. Every result still goes through clip and _repair, so the packings stay valid.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. With sd=0 the rotated start goes into SLSQP unchanged, and that is intended. The default sd=0.02 keeps the old behaviour on the other path.

My recomputed z is about 0.216, using diff 0.0009 and se = 0.0034*sqrt(1/1+1/2) ≈ 0.00416. The reported 0.222 probably comes from unrounded values. Either way it is far below any threshold, and there is only one candidate run, so reject is the right provisional decision.

Something to check, not a veto: the candidate's adjusted value of 2.9375 is above the best published value of about 2.9370 given in the card. A 3-seed mean above the best known optimum is surprising. It may only mean the card's figure is approximate, or that the 'adjusted' value includes noise. Check the raw per-seed sums and the exact validity check before trusting a gain this close to the optimum.
